reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll start by listing the refunds recorded there.
The ledger's refund list matches Alpha's handoff exactly (orders 320 and 325, same amounts). Next I should check the orders so I can confirm the refunds are consistent with them before paying.

The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff, and both refunds are below their order totals (320: 1313 of 11199; 325: 4296 of 9903), so nothing looks wrong. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 41189 matches my check: orders 320 and 323 total 42502, less the 1313 refund on order 320, gives 41189. Next I'll get birch's net balance.

Birch's net balance of 31975 matches my check: orders 321 and 324 total 31975, and birch has no refunds. Cobalt has a refund on order 325, so I'll get its net balance next to confirm the refund was applied correctly.

Cobalt's net balance of 9154 matches my check: orders 322 and 325 total 13450, less the 4296 refund on order 325, gives 9154. All three balances agree with the ledger, so Alpha's refund work looks complete and correct. I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 41189 is recorded. Birch's net balance of 31975 already matched my independent check against the orders and refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch payouts are recorded. Cobalt's net balance of 9154 already matched my independent check against orders 322 and 325 and the refund on 325, so I'll record that last payout.
All three payouts are recorded, and each matched my independent check against the orders and refunds. The task is complete, so I'll finish with the report.
